One restore-state regression was found at `eef4cfc3`: a keyboard backlight deliberately turned off after an earlier unlock can turn back on after the next lock/blank/unlock cycle.

## Preserve a user-selected zero across separate lock cycles

The new guard in [`bin/omarchy-brightness-keyboard`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/eef4cfc3f7d28655541563bb867f7ebd43ac6919/bin/omarchy-brightness-keyboard#L28-L37) treats every zero as an already-blanked backlight. However, `brightnessctl -r` retains its saved value, and the normal `down`/`cycle` commands do not replace it. After a previous lock saved a nonzero level, the next `off` skips saving a user-selected zero and `restore` brings back that older level.

A synthetic device with maximum brightness 100 reproduced this using the production command with a remapped LED path and a `brightnessctl` stub modeled on version 0.5.1:

```text
Sequence                               Base       PR
Start at 50; off; restore               50         50
--no-osd down five times                 0          0
off; restore                            0         50
```

The lock service invokes `off` when blanking and `omarchy-system-wake` invokes `restore`, so this maps to locking long enough to blank, unlocking, turning the keyboard light off, then repeating the lock/blank/unlock cycle.

**Impact:** the second cycle reverses the user's choice to leave the keyboard backlight off. This requires a prior nonzero saved level in the same login session.

**Suggested change:** distinguish a repeated blank within the same blank/restore cycle from a fresh cycle starting at a user-selected zero. Preserve zero on the latter path while retaining the repeated-`off` fix, and cover the sequence above in the regression test. Explicit per-device cycle state is one possible approach, not a verified patch.

**Verified:** the intended `77 → off → off → restore` sequence restores 77 on the PR and 0 on the base in the synthetic checks. The added test passes on the PR and fails on an equivalent baseline control at the second-`off` assertion.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** pinned base/head command checks with synthetic LEDs and stubbed `brightnessctl`; lock/wake callers and brightnessctl 0.5.1 save-file behavior inspected in source. No physical keyboard, native brightnessctl, running lock-screen session or broad shell-suite validation.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial inspection, independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, followed by source/evidence verification and post-review adjudication. A fresh Astra Medium check assessed presentation and disclosures, not technical correctness.
